title: the Skanda (Kartikeya)
tomorrow: why would a book named for a god read like a travel guide?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Garuda: a map, a mirror or a rite, and a book about the dead, read to the living in the chairs. Today, a new Purana, named for a god, and a birth.

At a family party, a newborn gets passed around the room: an aunt, a grandmother, a cousin, each one waiting for a turn. In one old story, six women who are also stars find a baby lying in a bed of reeds by a river, and every one of them wants to nurse him. There's one baby. Then he does something no ordinary baby can do. That's one telling of how Skanda, also called Kartikeya, came to be, and a whole Purana carries his name.
screen: `A BABY PASSED AROUND THE ROOM.` → `SIX STAR WOMEN, ONE BABY.` → `THEN HE DOES SOMETHING STRANGE.`

segments.voice: The tellings differ from text to text, but the shape is shared. The gods are in trouble. A demon, Taraka, can be beaten only by a son of Shiva, and Shiva is deep in meditation. When the son finally comes, he comes as fire, too fierce to hold. In several tellings it passes from Agni, the fire god, to the river Ganga, and comes to rest in a bed of reeds. There the Krittikas, star sisters, find him, and each wants to nurse him. So he grows six faces, one for each mother, and drinks from all of them, and the story says he's called Kartikeya because of them. He grows fast, leads the gods' army, and defeats Taraka. Feel the story's textures: fire too hot for any hand, cool river water, soft reeds, a baby's hunger. The fire nobody can hold gets passed along, hand to hand, until it can be a child. And the child no single mother could raise gets several, and instead of choosing, he becomes someone who can turn toward each of them. The warrior the gods are waiting for starts out as a baby who needs feeding. Today is the birth the Purana is named for: six faces, turned toward everyone who took care of him.
screen: `ONLY A SON OF SHIVA CAN WIN.` · `FIRE, RIVER, REEDS.` · `SIX FACES FOR SIX MOTHERS.` · then, large: `A FACE FOR EVERYONE WHO CARED.`

segments.voice: Sit tall, and turn your head slowly, a little to one side, then the other, then gently up and down. At each turn, bring to mind one person who helped raise you or look after you, and let your face rest toward them for a breath. If you pray, you can thank God for each of them.
The Skanda. The Purana named for Skanda, Shiva's son, called Kartikeya after the star sisters who nursed him.
Your line: the Skanda, Kartikeya. Six faces, one turned to each mother who came. More tomorrow.
